MERIDIAN CARD SERVICES — DISPUTES OPERATIONS
CASE REVIEW PACKET: DISPUTE DP-26-0703318 (PAXNET CREDIT CARD)

=== EXCERPT 1: PAXNET DISPUTE RULES FOR ISSUERS (EDITION APRIL 2026), CHAPTER 9 ===

9.0 General
9.0.1 The issuer may raise a dispute on behalf of a cardholder only under a valid reason code and within the time limits of that reason code. Rules in this chapter are to be applied by the issuer's dispute analyst at each stage (initial dispute, pre-arbitration). The analyst's decision at the representment review stage is whether the dispute is decided in the cardholder's favour (the provisional credit is made final and the merchant is debited) or in the merchant's favour (the provisional credit is reversed).
9.0.2 Days are calendar days unless stated otherwise.
9.0.3 A merchant's compelling evidence must be assessed against the specific requirements of the reason code; general statements ("the item was shipped", "the customer is a repeat buyer") are not compelling evidence.

9.1 Reason code 13.1 — Merchandise or services not received
9.1.1 Use: the cardholder paid for merchandise or services that were not received by the agreed date or location.
9.1.2 Pre-conditions: (a) the cardholder attempted to resolve the dispute with the merchant, and either the merchant refused, did not respond within 7 days, or the merchant is no longer trading; (b) the cardholder has not received the merchandise at the time of the dispute.
9.1.3 Time limit: the dispute must be raised within 120 days of the expected delivery date where the purchase terms stated an expected delivery date or a latest delivery date; otherwise within 120 days of the transaction processing date. In any case not later than 540 days after the transaction processing date.
9.1.4 Merchant compelling evidence (representment) is limited to:
   (a) proof of delivery to the address given by the cardholder at the time of purchase, such as carrier tracking showing delivery to that address;
   (b) proof of delivery to a collection point, parcel locker or other pickup location, but only where (i) the cardholder selected that pickup location at checkout or later authorised the change in writing, or (ii) the merchant also provides evidence that the cardholder or a person authorised by the cardholder collected the item (for example a locker log showing collection with the cardholder's PIN, or a signed pickup receipt);
   (c) evidence that the cardholder has used the merchandise or services (for example online account activity for digital goods);
   (d) evidence that the cardholder agreed to a new delivery date that has not yet passed.
9.1.5 A carrier-initiated redirection of a parcel (for example after a failed delivery attempt) does not by itself constitute the cardholder's selection or authorisation of the pickup location, even if the carrier notified the cardholder by email or text message.
9.1.6 A merchant offer to re-ship or refund made after the dispute has been raised does not invalidate the dispute unless the cardholder accepts it.

9.2 Reason code 13.3 — Not as described or defective merchandise
9.2.1 The cardholder must have returned or attempted to return the merchandise, unless the merchant refused to provide return instructions.
9.2.2 Time limit: 120 days from the date of receipt of the merchandise.

9.3 Reason code 13.6 — Credit not processed
9.3.1 Use where the merchant provided a credit voucher or a refund acknowledgement that was not processed. Time limit: 120 days from the date on the credit acknowledgement; if undated, 120 days from the date of the cardholder's return of the goods.

Post-incident severity review for INC-2026-0908-114 ("Invoice API elevated 5xx, eu-west")

======================================================================
(A) INCIDENT SEVERITY RUNBOOK ISR v5.0 (effective 1 February 2026)
======================================================================
1. Purpose
1.1 The severity of an incident determines paging, communication cadence, executive notification and the post-incident review format. The final severity is set at the post-incident review according to this runbook, based on the facts established after the incident; the severity declared during the incident is provisional.
1.2 This runbook covers availability, performance and data incidents. Security incidents (suspected or confirmed unauthorised access, data exfiltration, credential compromise) are classified under SICS-2 instead; where an incident is both, the higher of the two severities applies.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Active tenant" — a tenant that sent at least one API request in the 7 days before the incident started.
2.2 "Affected tenant" — an active tenant for which more than 5 % of its API requests failed (5xx or timeout) in at least one 10-minute monitoring window during the incident. Tenants with some failed requests below that rate in every window are not affected tenants.
2.3 "Enterprise tenant" — a tenant on an Enterprise plan with a signed Enterprise Master Services Agreement. Tenants on an Enterprise Trial (evaluation) plan are not Enterprise tenants for the purposes of this runbook.
2.4 "Payment processing" — the authorisation, capture, refund and payout APIs, and the ledger writes behind them. Invoicing, billing documents (invoice PDFs, statements), reporting and the merchant dashboard are not payment processing.
2.5 "Incident duration" — the time from the start of the first 10-minute monitoring window in which the incident's failure criterion was met to the end of the last such window. Alerting, acknowledgement and verification times are not part of the incident duration.
2.6 "Workaround" — a documented alternative that allows affected tenants to complete the affected operation without LatticePay intervention (e.g. a fallback endpoint), communicated to them on the status page or directly.
2.7 "Data loss" — loss of data that LatticePay had acknowledged as received. Data that can be restored automatically from the write-ahead log or replayed from the event archive, without manual reconstruction and with no more than 15 minutes of data affected, is "recoverable within RPO".

3. Base severity (impact)
3.1 SEV-1: more than 40 % of active tenants affected; or any unrecoverable data loss; or complete unavailability of payment processing in any region for 5 minutes or more.
3.2 SEV-2: more than 10 % and up to 40 % of active tenants affected; or 3 or more Enterprise tenants affected.
3.3 SEV-3: at least 1 % and up to 10 % of active tenants affected; or 1 or 2 Enterprise tenants affected.
3.4 SEV-4: fewer than 1 % of active tenants affected and no Enterprise tenant affected.
3.5 Where several criteria apply, the highest resulting severity is the base severity.

4. Adjustments (applied to the base severity in this order)
4.1 Duration: if the incident duration is more than 4 hours, raise the severity by one level (SEV-4 → SEV-3, SEV-3 → SEV-2, SEV-2 → SEV-1).
4.2 Workaround: if a Workaround was available to all affected tenants for the whole incident duration after the first 30 minutes, lower the severity by one level.
4.3 An adjustment never moves the severity above SEV-1 or below SEV-4.

5. Communication by severity
5.1 SEV-1: status page within 15 minutes; updates every 30 minutes; executive on-call paged; customer RCA within 5 business days.
5.2 SEV-2: status page within 30 minutes; updates hourly; customer RCA within 10 business days.
5.3 SEV-3: status page if more than 20 tenants affected; internal review only.
5.4 SEV-4: no status page; ticket-level follow-up.

6. Roles
6.1 Incident commander (IC): declares provisional severity, coordinates responders.
6.2 Communications lead: status page and Enterprise account managers.
6.3 Scribe: timeline in the incident channel.
6.4 Service owner: confirms the technical facts used for the final severity (affected tenants, duration, data impact) in writing before the review.
6.5 The IC's provisional severity is not changed during the incident for reclassification purposes; reclassification happens only at the review.

7. Post-incident review
7.1 A post-incident review is held within 5 business days for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents and within 15 business days for SEV-3. SEV-4 incidents are reviewed in the weekly operations meeting.
7.2 The review records the final severity, the facts on which it is based and the corrective actions.
7.3 Final severity drives the reliability scorecard: SEV-1 = 10 points, SEV-2 = 5, SEV-3 = 2, SEV-4 = 0.

8. Historical note
8.1 ISR v4.2 (in force until 31 January 2026) used "tenants with any failed request" as affected tenants and treated Enterprise Trial tenants as Enterprise tenants. It had no workaround adjustment and no floors.

INC-2026-0322-067 | ISR v5.0 | 44 affected of 3,950 (1.1 %) | 0 Enterprise | 2 h 10 min | Workaround from 00:12 | SEV-4
INC-2026-0611-088 | ISR v5.0 + CN-5.1 | Payouts API degraded 22 min, 0.8 % affected | SEV-2 (payment processing floor)

CHANGE NOTICE CN-5.1 (approved by the Reliability Council, effective 1 June 2026)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
CN-5.1.1 New section 4.4: "Floor for Enterprise impact. After the adjustments in 4.1 and 4.2, an incident in which at least one Enterprise tenant was affected is never below SEV-3."
CN-5.1.2 New section 3.6: "Payment processing floor. Any incident in which payment processing was degraded (more than 5 % failed requests in a 10-minute window) for 15 minutes or more is at least SEV-2 before adjustments."

======================================================================
S1 Any confirmed unauthorised access to cardholder data: S-1 (maps to SEV-1).

S3 Vulnerability discovered without evidence of exploitation: S-3 (maps to SEV-3).

======================================================================
Invoice API — generates invoice documents (PDF/UBL) for merchants' customers and stores them in the document store. Part of the Billing Documents product.
Payments API — authorisation, capture, refund; Payouts API — merchant settlements.

(D) INCIDENT TIMELINE (UTC) AND MONITORING
======================================================================
8 September 2026
13:31 Deployment of document-store client library 4.12.0 to Invoice API pods in eu-west.
13:40–13:50 First 10-minute monitoring window in which the Invoice API 5xx rate exceeded 5 % for affected tenants.

14:47 Webhook dispatcher backlog; 11 minutes of "invoice.rendered" events (14:36–14:47) dropped from the in-memory queue during a pod restart.
15:10 Event replay from the event archive started automatically for 14:36–14:47; completed 15:18; no manual steps.
16:55 Rollback to library 4.11.3 started.
17:30–17:40 Last 10-minute monitoring window with 5xx rate above 5 %.
17:51 IC declared all-clear after verification.
Security: on 9 September a routine security review ticket SEC-REV-2231 was opened "as standard follow-up to any library-related incident"; no unauthorised access suspected; closed 11 September with no findings.

======================================================================
(E) CUSTOMER IMPACT DATA (analytics export, 10 September 2026)
======================================================================
Active tenants (at least one request in the 7 days before 13:31 on 8 September): 4,020. Provisioned tenants (all, including dormant): 5,610.
Tenants with at least one failed Invoice API request during the incident: 455.
Tenants with more than 5 % of API requests failed in at least one 10-minute window: 318.
Enterprise-plan tenants among the 318:
  T-10044 Moravia Retail Group — Enterprise plan, Enterprise MSA signed 2023.
  T-11820 Kestrel Hospitality — Enterprise plan, Enterprise MSA signed March 2026.
  T-12977 Orinoco Sports GmbH — Enterprise Trial plan (evaluation until 30 September 2026); MSA under negotiation.
Enterprise-plan tenants among the 137 tenants with failures below 5 % in every window: T-10390 Harwell Foods (Enterprise, MSA 2024).
Payments API volume during the incident: normal; no tenant had payment failures above baseline.

======================================================================
(F) ON-CALL NOTES
======================================================================
IC handover note (18:05): "Total impact roughly 4 h 10 min from first alert to all-clear. Three Enterprise customers affected, 455 tenants saw errors. Webhook events lost for 11 min but replayed. Suggest keeping SEV-2 for the review."
Communications lead: status page updates posted 14:02, 14:08, 15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 17:55. Account managers of T-10044, T-11820 and T-12977 informed.
Root-cause summary (engineering, 10 September): "Library 4.12.0 changed the default connection-pool size for the document store from 64 to 8. Under normal afternoon load, render requests queued and timed out after 30 s, returning 504. The synchronous v1 endpoint uses a separate pool and was unaffected. The in-memory webhook queue lost events on the pod restart at 14:47 because the graceful-shutdown hook was also affected; the archive-based replay worked as designed."
Corrective actions proposed: pin pool size in configuration; canary deployments for library upgrades; alert threshold review.

PART 1 — CUSTOMER DATA HANDLING STANDARD CDH-4 (v3.1)

§1 Scope
1.1 CDH-4 governs how Brightwater stores, uses, restricts and erases personal data of customers of the web shop and the retail stores.
1.2 Employee data, supplier contacts and job applicants are covered by separate standards (HR-7, PRC-2, TA-3).
1.3 Where CDH-4 requires a record to be "restricted", the record is moved to the restricted archive: it is kept, but may only be accessed by Finance, Legal or Privacy for the purpose for which it is retained, and it is excluded from marketing, analytics and customer service tools.

§2 Definitions
2.1 "Customer" — a natural person with a web-shop account or a loyalty card, identified by a Customer ID in the CRM.
2.2 "Account Data" — name, contact details, login credentials, saved addresses, saved payment tokens, preferences and loyalty data.
2.3 "Order Data" — baskets, quotes, order confirmations, delivery tracking and order-related customer service notes.
2.4 "Transaction Record" — the record of a completed sale for which an invoice was issued: the invoice itself, the corresponding payment record and the delivery confirmation. Baskets, quotes, pro-forma documents and orders cancelled before an invoice was issued are not Transaction Records, even if a payment was authorised and later released. A pro-forma document is not an invoice.
2.5 "Warranty Record" — product registration and warranty claim data needed to handle a warranty claim for a product sold to the Customer.
2.6 "Marketing Data" — newsletter subscription, consent log, campaign responses, segmentation attributes.
2.7 "Legal Hold" — an instruction from Legal to preserve all data relating to a specified Customer ID (or IDs) because of actual or anticipated litigation, a regulatory inquiry or a payment dispute.
2.8 "Verified Request" — a request that meets the verification requirements of §3.
2.9 "Invoice date" — the date printed on the invoice as its date of issue. It may differ from the order date and from the delivery date.

§3 Verification of requests
3.1 A request is verified if it is (a) submitted through the privacy form while the Customer is logged into the account, or (b) sent by e-mail from the e-mail address registered on the account and confirmed by the Customer through the six-digit code sent to that address.
3.2 A request sent from any other e-mail address or by post is verified only when the requester provides two of the following that match the CRM: an order number, the billing postcode, the loyalty card number, the last four digits of a saved card.
3.3 A request made by a third party on behalf of a Customer requires a signed authority from the Customer in addition to verification under 3.1 or 3.2.
3.4 Until a request is verified, no action is taken on it other than asking for verification. The response deadline in §7 runs from the date of verification.

§4 Erasure requests
4.1 On a Verified Request for erasure, Brightwater erases all personal data relating to the Customer ID, subject only to 4.2 to 4.4.
4.2 Legal Hold. While a Legal Hold covering the Customer ID is active, nothing is erased; all data relating to that Customer ID is restricted until the hold is released, and the request is then processed under 4.1.
4.3 Transaction Records whose retention period (§5) has not ended on the day the erasure is carried out are not erased but restricted; they are erased at the end of the retention period without a further request.
4.4 Warranty Records are retained (restricted) while the warranty period for the product plus six months is running.
4.5 Marketing Data is always erased immediately; the Customer's e-mail address is added to the suppression list in hashed form so that it is not re-imported from partner lists. The hashed suppression entry is not personal data held about the Customer for the purposes of 4.1.
4.6 An erasure request is not refused because the Customer has an open balance; Finance is informed and collects on the basis of the Transaction Records.
4.7 Loyalty points lapse on erasure. The Customer is told this in the acknowledgement.

§5 Retention periods
5.1 Transaction Records: ten (10) years from the end of the calendar year in which the invoice date falls.
5.2 Warranty Records: the warranty period of the product plus six months.
5.3 Customer service tickets not related to an order: three years from closure.
5.4 CCTV images from stores: 72 hours, unless a Legal Hold applies.

§6 Legal holds
6.1 Legal Holds are entered in the Legal Hold register by Legal, identifying the Customer ID(s) covered. A hold covers only the Customer IDs listed.
6.2 A Legal Hold remains active until Legal records its release in the register. Once released, the Customer's data is handled under the normal rules; release does not revive or cancel any pending request.

§7 Response deadline
7.1 Erasure is carried out and confirmed to the Customer within 30 days of the Verified Request.
7.2 Erased data may persist in encrypted backups for up to 35 days until the backup cycle overwrites it. This is not a ground for refusing or delaying erasure.

§8 Refusal
8.1 An erasure request may only be refused if it is manifestly unfounded or excessive (e.g. repeated identical requests within 3 months), as decided by the Data Protection Officer.

§9 Business accounts
9.1 For business accounts (account type "B2B" in the CRM), contact persons' data is erased on request, but Transaction Records of the business are retained for ten (10) years from the end of the calendar year of the invoice date regardless of Amendment 2026-1, because business customers' invoices are also retained under the commercial record-keeping rules of the purchaser's contract.

§10 Access and portability requests
10.1 On a Verified Request for access, Brightwater provides a copy of all personal data relating to the Customer ID within 30 days, including restricted records, in a commonly used electronic format.
10.2 Portability exports cover Account Data and Order Data provided by the Customer; derived segmentation attributes are excluded.
10.3 An access request made together with an erasure request is answered first; erasure follows once the export has been downloaded or 14 days after it was made available, whichever is earlier.

§11 Rectification and objection
11.1 Inaccurate Account Data is corrected within 10 days of a Verified Request.
11.2 An objection to marketing is handled as a request to erase Marketing Data only (4.5 applies); other data is not affected unless the Customer also requests erasure.
11.3 Where a Customer's wording is unclear ("stop contacting me", "remove me from your lists"), Privacy asks whether erasure of the whole account is intended before acting beyond 11.2.

§12 Store purchases without account
12.1 Receipts of store purchases paid by card are Transaction Records of the store; they are linked to a Customer ID only where a loyalty card was scanned.
12.2 Store purchases with a loyalty card scan appear in the ERP under the Customer ID with document type "POS".

AMENDMENT 2026-1 TO CDH-4 (approved by the Data Protection Officer and the CFO, effective 1 January 2026)

(1) COMMERCIAL RETURNS POLICY CRP-5

§1 Scope
1.1 CRP-5 applies to returns by business customers of products bought directly from Corvid. Products bought through distributors are returned to the distributor under the distributor's terms.
1.2 Warranty claims under the Corvid Limited Warranty (24 months) are handled separately by the Service department; a return under CRP-5 is a commercial return (return for credit) and does not affect warranty rights.

§2 Definitions
2.1 "Standard Product" — a product listed in the Corvid catalogue, supplied in a catalogue configuration.
2.2 "Custom-built Product" — a product built to the customer's specification, including any product whose configuration was not available in the catalogue, products with customer-specific firmware, labelling or housings, and products ordered under a project quotation.
2.3 "Delivery Date" — the date on which the goods were delivered to the customer's delivery address, as shown by the carrier's proof of delivery. The dispatch date and the invoice date are not the Delivery Date.
2.4 "RMA Request Date" — the date on which the customer submits a complete return request in the Corvid partner portal (order number, items, quantities and reason).
2.5 "Defective" — a product in which Corvid's inspection confirms a fault in materials or workmanship present at delivery. A product returned as defective in which the inspection finds no fault ("No Fault Found", NFF) is not Defective.
2.6 "Unused" — not installed in a powered application for more than 72 hours in total, with no physical damage, and returned with all accessories.

§3 Return window and eligibility
3.1 Standard Products may be returned for credit if the RMA Request Date is no later than 30 days after the Delivery Date and the products are Unused, or are Defective.
3.2 Custom-built Products are not returnable for credit. Defective Custom-built Products are repaired or replaced under 5.3.
3.3 Returns of Standard Products requested more than 30 days after the Delivery Date are rejected, unless the products are Defective (5.3 applies).
3.4 Minimum return value: EUR 100 per RMA.

§4 Credit
4.1 Returns accepted under 3.1 are credited at the invoiced net price.
4.2 A restocking fee of 15 % of the credited value is deducted for returns that are not Defective.
4.3 The restocking fee is waived (a) for Gold partners; (b) where the return results from a Corvid shipping or order-entry error; (c) for products discontinued by Corvid within 60 days before the RMA Request Date.
4.4 Freight for returns that are not Defective is paid by the customer.
4.5 No restocking fee may be waived other than under 4.3, except with the written approval of the Head of Customer Service.
4.6 Credits are calculated per RMA; partial returns of an order line are credited pro rata.

§5 Defective products
5.1 Products returned as Defective are inspected within 10 business days of receipt.
5.2 Defective Standard Products returned within the 30-day window are credited in full (no restocking fee); outside the window they are repaired or replaced.
5.3 Defective Custom-built Products are repaired or replaced; no credit is given.
5.4 NFF returns are treated as returns that are not Defective. Eligibility and credit are assessed under §3 and §4 as at the RMA Request Date.

§6 Process
6.1 Goods must not be sent back without an RMA number.
6.2 The returns desk issues its decision (credit with or without fee, repair/replace, or rejection) after inspection.
6.3 Goods returned without an RMA number, or more than 15 days after the RMA number was issued, may be refused at the warehouse.
6.4 The customer bears the risk of loss in transit for returns that are not Defective.

§7 Special cases
7.1 Demonstration units lent to customers are not sales and are returned under the loan agreement.
7.2 Trade-in programme: customers replacing CX-200 controllers with CX-400 controllers may return the old units for a trade-in credit of EUR 150 per unit within 90 days of the CX-400 delivery; trade-ins are not returns under CRP-5.
7.3 Software licences and firmware upgrade keys are not returnable once activated.
7.4 Spare parts ordered through the Service department are returned under the Service terms.

§8 Credit notes
8.1 Credit notes are issued in the currency of the original invoice within 10 business days of the returns desk decision.
8.2 Credit notes are offset against open invoices first; any balance is paid out on request.
8.3 Restocking fees are shown as a separate line on the credit note.

§9 Returns from outside the EU
9.1 Customers outside the EU must return goods with export documentation marking them as returned goods; customs duties charged on re-import are deducted from the credit unless the return is Defective.
9.2 Norway: returns are processed with a T1 transit document; no import duty is charged on returned Corvid goods of EU origin if the documentation is correct.

§10 Relationship with the Limited Warranty
10.1 A customer whose return request is rejected under §3 keeps any warranty rights for Defective products.
10.2 Products found NFF under a warranty claim are returned to the customer at the customer's cost; an inspection fee of EUR 60 per unit may be charged under the Service terms.

PAYMENT RELIEF POLICY PR-5 (EXTRACT), AMENDMENT PR-5/A1, AND APPLICATION FILE PRA-2026-02917

=== PAYMENT RELIEF POLICY PR-5 (VERSION 3, 1 FEBRUARY 2025) ===

1. Purpose
PR-5 sets the conditions under which Brackwater offers a temporary Payment Relief Plan (reduced monthly payments for up to six months, with the shortfall added to the balance) to residential mortgage customers in financial difficulty. Customers who do not qualify are still offered the standard arrears support options in policy PR-2 (payment arrangements, term extensions, referral to free debt advice). PR-5 decisions must be consistent and evidence-based; case handlers may not waive any eligibility condition.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Household" — the borrowers named on the mortgage and their spouses or partners living at the mortgaged property.
2.2 "Gross Monthly Income" — the total income of the Household before tax and deductions in a calendar month, including salary, wages, self-employed drawings, pensions and regular benefits. It excludes one-off payments: annual or discretionary bonuses, redundancy lump sums, gifts, inheritances, and tax refunds.
2.3 "Hardship Event" — a change of circumstances that reduces Household income, such as job loss, reduction of hours, illness, bereavement or relationship breakdown. The "Hardship Month" is the calendar month in which the Hardship Event occurred.
2.4 "Baseline Income" — the average Gross Monthly Income over the full calendar months immediately before the Hardship Month (the number of months is set in clause 3.1(a)).

Exact duplicates are each responsive when stored in separate systems unless the hold notice permits deduplication. "Derived analytics" are records produced from source data; they are not source records. "Verified deletion" means deletion from active systems and expiration from ordinary backups under the stated schedule, with a logged confirmation. Cryptographic erasure counts only if the relevant keys exclusively protect the named records.

3. Customer requests. A verified identity request is due within 30 calendar days. Data needed for contract performance may be retained while necessary. Data under legal hold is retained even after the ordinary purpose ends, and the customer receives the standard limitation notice. Non-held data in the same account remains subject to deletion.

DEFINITIONS
In this policy, "you" and "your" refer to the named insured shown in the Declarations and the spouse if a resident of the same household. "We", "us" and "our" refer to the company providing this insurance.

1. "Bodily injury" means bodily harm, sickness or disease, including required care, loss of services and death that results.
2. "Business" means a trade, profession or occupation engaged in on a full-time, part-time or occasional basis, or any other activity engaged in for money or other compensation, subject to the exceptions in Section II.
3. "Concealed water" means water or steam that escapes from within a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or automatic fire protective sprinkler system, or from within a household appliance, and that remains hidden within the walls, floors or ceilings of the dwelling, where the presence of such water was not known to and could not reasonably have been known to an "insured" before the damage became visible.
4. "Insured" means you and residents of your household who are your relatives, or other persons under the age of 21 and in the care of any person named above.
5. "Occurrence" means an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions, which results during the policy period in bodily injury or property damage.
6. "Repeated seepage or leakage" means continuous or repeated seepage or leakage of water or steam over a period of 14 or more days.
7. "Residence premises" means the one-family dwelling where you reside and which is shown as the residence premises in the Declarations.
8. "Unoccupied" means the dwelling contains contents, including furnishings and personal property, sufficient to support customary occupancy, but no person is living in it.
9. "Vacant" means the dwelling lacks contents, including furnishings and personal property, sufficient to support customary occupancy, whether or not a person is present. A dwelling under construction is not considered vacant.

SECTION I — PROPERTY COVERAGES
Coverage A — Dwelling. We cover the dwelling on the residence premises, including structures attached to the dwelling, and materials and supplies located on or next to the residence premises used to construct, alter or repair the dwelling.
Coverage B — Other Structures. We cover other structures on the residence premises set apart from the dwelling by clear space. Structures connected to the dwelling by only a fence, utility line or similar connection are considered other structures.
Coverage C — Personal Property. We cover personal property owned or used by an insured while it is anywhere in the world. Special limits apply to money ($200), securities ($1,500), watercraft ($1,500), trailers ($1,500), theft of jewelry ($1,500), theft of firearms ($2,500), and theft of silverware ($2,500).
Coverage D — Loss of Use. If a loss covered under Section I makes the residence premises not fit to live in, we cover any necessary increase in living expenses incurred by you so that your household can maintain its normal standard of living.

SECTION I — PERILS INSURED AGAINST
We insure against direct physical loss to property described in Coverages A and B, except as limited or excluded in this policy.
Accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam from within a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or automatic fire protective sprinkler system or from within a household appliance is covered, subject to the exclusions and limits below. We also pay the reasonable cost of tearing out and replacing any part of a building necessary to repair the system or appliance from which the water or steam escaped; we do not pay for the system or appliance itself.

SECTION I — EXCLUSIONS
4.1 Earth Movement. Earthquake, landslide, mudflow, subsidence or sinkhole, unless direct loss by fire or explosion ensues.
4.2 Freezing. Freezing of a plumbing, heating, air conditioning or sprinkler system or a household appliance while the dwelling is vacant or unoccupied, unless you have used reasonable care to maintain heat in the building or to shut off the water supply and drain all systems and appliances.
4.3 Repeated Seepage or Leakage. We do not cover loss caused by "repeated seepage or leakage" of water or steam.
    4.3.1 Exception for concealed water. Exclusion 4.3 does not apply to loss caused by "concealed water". Our total payment for all loss caused by concealed water in any one occurrence will not exceed $10,000, including the cost of tearing out and replacing any part of the building. This limit does not increase the Coverage A limit.
4.4 Wear and Tear. Wear and tear, marring, deterioration; mechanical breakdown, latent defect, inherent vice; smog, rust or other corrosion. However, if one of these causes the accidental discharge of water or steam, we cover the resulting water damage to the building, subject to 4.3 and 4.7; we do not cover the corroded pipe itself.
4.5 Neglect. Neglect of an insured to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property at and after the time of a loss.
4.6 Ordinance or Law. Enforcement of any ordinance or law regulating construction, repair or demolition, except as provided under Additional Coverages.
4.7 Vacancy. We do not cover loss caused by vandalism, malicious mischief, glass breakage, or any accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam, if the dwelling has been vacant for more than 60 consecutive days immediately before the loss.
4.8 Intentional Loss. Any loss arising out of any act an insured commits or conspires to commit with the intent to cause a loss.

SECTION I — CONDITIONS
Duties After Loss. In case of a loss to covered property, you must see that the following are done: give prompt notice to us or our agent; protect the property from further damage and make reasonable and necessary repairs to protect it; keep an accurate record of repair expenses; prepare an inventory of damaged personal property; as often as we reasonably require, show the damaged property and submit to examination under oath; send us within 60 days after our request your signed, sworn proof of loss.
Loss Settlement. Buildings under Coverage A are settled at replacement cost without deduction for depreciation, subject to the limits and sublimits of this policy, provided you actually repair or replace the damaged building within 180 days after the loss.
Deductible. SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(i.id) AS paid_invoice_count
```sql
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN invoices AS i ON i.customer_id = c.id
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
  AND i.issued_at >= DATE '2025-01-01'
  AND i.issued_at <  DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY c.id;
```
`COUNT(i.id)` avoids counting the NULL-extended row produced by the outer join.
